1.he: ירושלמי חגיגה פ"א ה"א ומגילה פ"ד ה"א
1.note: Weiss writes "halakhah 1" for both places. In the usual numbering of the Yerushalmi the saying is at Ḥagigah 1:8 and Megillah 4:1; the English gives those.

2.note: The print has Yosifon, the Hebrew name used in Weiss's time for Josephus as well as for the medieval Sefer Yosippon. The statement that the Sadducees rejected the tradition of the elders is from Josephus, Antiquities 13.297, so the English gives Josephus.

3.note: The Cyrus story is in Josephus, Antiquities 11.1.2, not book 2, ch. 1; kept as printed.

4.note: Zechariah son of Jeberechiah is in Isaiah 8:2; the print has ה' ב' (5:2), likely ח read as ה by the printer; kept as printed.

5.note: Literally 'foundations of the existing'; rendered as existing practice.

6.note: The verse on keeping God's statutes is Genesis 26:5; the print has 27:5; kept as printed.

7.note: Word clear in the scan but unusual; read as from מחיה, 'livelihood'.

8.note: Niebuhr's work on Arabia (probably *Beschreibung von Arabien*); Weiss gives no exact title.

9.note: Joab at the altar is 1 Kings 2:28–34; מ"ב may mean Kings, chapter 2 or 2 Kings 2; kept as printed.

10.note: The quoted words 'as I have commanded you' are in Deuteronomy 12:21; kept as printed.

11.note: Singular 'he knew' in the print, where the sense requires 'they knew'; translated as printed.

12.note: Graetz's commentary on Ecclesiastes (1871) already dates the book to the time of Herod; the year 1889 refers to a later article in his monthly journal. The scan is of a later printing, which updates such references (it also cites vols. 4 and 5 of this work). The English keeps the printed year.

13.note: The figures of these two references are printed left to right inside the Hebrew line and are partly blurred in the scan; the reading 42:22 and 64:9–10 is the most likely one.

14.note: the second figure is printed מ"א; perhaps for a halakhah or section number.

15.note: the second letter is unclear in the scan (כ or ב); read as 124.
